Bottom lineall findings below are fixed in the repo (41 tests pass), except README drift (10), which is accepted. Only the Copilot smoke test is still open.

High env git push --force passes the guard; git -P push skips the ask

Problem
no decision for env git push --force, git -P push or GIT_TRACE=1 git push. Claude's deny rule also misses it.
Fix
strip a leading env, VAR=value and git's valueless options (-P, --paginate, --no-optional-locks) before the checks; add tests.
If skipped
a push written this way gets no hard stop and no ask.
Where
guard.mjs:29, guard.mjs:251, guard.mjs:254

Medium The guard allows any call whose input is not valid JSON

Problem
readInput() returns null on a parse error, and null means no decision. With a BOM in front (as PowerShell 5.1 pipes it), git push --force passed.
Fix
strip a leading BOM. Input that is not empty but does not parse is a deny.
If skipped
a tool that sends a BOM turns the guard off silently.
Where
guard.mjs:412-414, hooks/claude/hook.mjs:9

Medium The Kiro permissions merge can write a file Kiro rejects, with no backup

Problem
rules: [], rules: # note and a list at indent 0 (rules:\n- capability: …) all come out as a second rules: key or as a list with mixed indents. User-level settings files are rewritten with no copy.
Fix
write rules: [] when empty, write via temp file and rename, back up user files first, and skip unknown rules: shapes.
If skipped
one install can lock Kiro out of every tool, with no way back.
Where
install.mjs:253, install.mjs:261, install.mjs:426-444
